title: Get, set, and count
hints: A dict from key to value handles `set`, `get`, and `delete` directly. `dict.get(key)` already returns None for missing keys.
`count` can scan `self.data.values()`, but databases answer it from an index. Keep a second dict, `value -> number of keys holding it`, next to the data.

Every write touches the index twice: on `set`, decrement the old value's count (if the key existed) and increment the new one; on `delete`, decrement the removed value. A `collections.Counter` makes the bookkeeping short.
Overwriting a key with the value it already has must leave `count` unchanged. Decrement-then-increment handles that for free.
